I been farming this land for 26 years. My father farmed it before me. I do not need to think too hard about what to do — I mostly do what I did last year, and what my neighbor Old Liu does. He has a bigger field than me but our land is the same soil.

My 7 mu I split like this: 5 mu I do wheat and then maize on the same field, one after another every year. The other 2 mu I keep for cotton. Cotton is more trouble — more spraying, more watering, more work — but it brings in cash money. If I lose cotton I lose cash. If I lose wheat, that is very bad, that is food and money both. So I am more careful with wheat.

**Wheat (5 mu, plant October):** I buy the improved seed from the township store, the same kind Old Liu uses. He got a good harvest last year. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant — the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kg bag. Then in March or April when the wheat gets to my knee, I spread about 15 kg of urea per mu. That is what everyone around here does. Three times I pull water from the well: once in November before it gets cold, once in April at the jointing time, once in May when the heads are filling out. I spray twice — once for weeds in winter, once for the white powder on the leaves in spring if I see it.

**Maize (5 mu, plant June right after wheat):** Same day I finish cutting wheat, almost same day I plant maize. No plowing — I just plant right into the stubble. The dealer knows me, I buy hybrid seeds from him every year, same brand as before. For fertilizer, I put a small amount of compound down at planting, then I top-dress with urea twice — once when the plant is knee-high, once before it tassels. Maize here does not need as much water if July and August have rain, but I irrigate at least twice to be safe. I spray maybe twice — once for the corn borer worm, once for weeds early.

**Cotton (2 mu, plant April-May):** I plow this field in spring, turn the soil over properly. Cotton I put compound fertilizer down when I transplant or when seedlings are up. Then I add urea two more times when the bolls are setting — that is when cotton needs feeding most. Cotton gets aphids, gets bollworm, gets whitefly — I spray four times through the season, sometimes more if I see trouble. I irrigate five times, especially at flowering and boll-set. Cotton is the most work on my farm.

I do not change much from last year. Prices for urea went up a bit, but I will not cut back on fertilizer for wheat — I would rather spend more and get a full harvest than save money and lose yield. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.
